🇺🇸🪖 How US push for Hezbollah disarmament is dragging Lebanon into a civil war
The US is pressing the Lebanese army to act decisively against Hezbollah's weapons, while the group refuses to give up its arsenal as long as Israeli forces remain on Lebanese soil. Together, these pressures could set Lebanon ablaze from within, The Cradle reports.
👉 The army leadership, however, is reluctant to launch a full-scale operation against Hezbollah's military structure. Estimates put the Lebanese Armed Forces at roughly 60,000 active personnel, backed by aging M48 and M60 tanks, limited artillery, and no effective air defense — a force that would struggle against Hezbollah's vast rocket arsenal and thousands of anti-tank systems and attack drones.
Beyond the immediate danger of armed confrontation, the US-brokered campaign could pull Lebanon's political and sectarian fault lines into the military itself, breaking apart an institution that has spent decades holding a fragile national balance together.
The internal challenge coincides with a major change in the south
🌏 A UN Security Council resolution ordered the steady withdrawal of the UNIFIL peacekeeping contingent, which served as an impartial observer and mediator that helped prevent accidental clashes and documented violations in southern Lebanon
🌏 Its departure leaves Lebanon alone with the Israeli army, which has still not fulfilled its obligations to withdraw troops from the south of the country

🇮🇷 Iran expects imminent attack, orders forces to activate ‘Mosaic Defense’ — report
Tehran now assumes a US-Israeli attack is coming and views Washington's diplomatic gestures as "unreliable", a senior Iranian security official told Fars News.
👉 Operational units have been instructed that if a new large-scale war erupts — including assassinations of Iranian officials or killings of civilians — they should treat US political assets and the infrastructure of countries participating in the conflict as "legitimate targets", the report added.
Iran already considers itself at war with the US, viewing the naval blockade and airspace restrictions as a continuation of the military aggression that began on February 28, the official was quoted as saying.
📑 [Iran’s ‘Mosaic Defense’ doctrine ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65841)is designed to ensure Iran can keep fighting even if its central leadership is decapitated. The IRGC has been restructured into 31 largely autonomous provincial commands, each with its own weapons stockpiles, logistics and decision-making authority — allowing commanders to launch missile and drone strikes without waiting for orders from Tehran.
